title: Beyond Linear Dynamics: Neural Bilinear Dynamical Models for Time Series Forecasting

problem.claim: Accurate forecasting is challenging when real-world time series are generated by nonlinear dynamical systems.

gap.claim: Existing dynamics-modeling approaches based on linear assumptions or Koopman-based linearizations may inadequately capture complex nonlinear behavior and accumulate errors in long-horizon prediction.

contributions.claim: The Neural Bilinear Dynamical Model models nonlinear system dynamics through a bilinear latent dynamical formulation.
NBDM incorporates a parameterized error compensation term to mitigate approximation error from bilinear representations.
NBDM explicitly integrates control inputs and uses a memory-enhanced controller to infer latent controls when inputs are missing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five real-world datasets reportedly show that NBDM consistently outperforms competitive baselines in given-control and missing-control settings, especially for multi-step and long-horizon forecasting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Nonlinear real-world dynamics make accurate time series forecasting difficult.
Linear and Koopman-based approaches may fail to capture complex nonlinear behavior and may accumulate long-horizon prediction errors.
NBDM lifts nonlinear dynamics into a latent space and models state evolution with bilinear dynamics, error compensation, and explicit or inferred controls.
The authors report improvements over competitive baselines across five real-world datasets and both control settings.

source_observation.claim: The method combines latent-space lifting, bilinear dynamics, error compensation, and control handling.

interpretation.claim: Forecasting models for nonlinear systems may benefit from separating representation, dynamics approximation, approximation-error correction, and control inference.

application.claim: This design can be considered for multi-step forecasting problems with nonlinear dynamics and partially missing control inputs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported datasets or control settings.
